title: Carpentry Program Celebrates First Graduating Class in Tennessee
summary: Trousdale Turner Correctional Center and the Tennessee College of Applied Technology celebrate their first cohort of carpentry program graduates.
body_text: Residents at CoreCivic's Trousdale Turner Correctional Center in Hartsville, Tennessee, are celebrating their graduation from the new Tennessee College of Applied Technology (TCAT) carpentry program. This is the program's first graduating class. The program offers participants job-ready skills and certifications, helping them secure a job upon release and reduce recidivism. TCAT focuses on vocational skills like carpentry with plans to expand to additional fields including plumbing and electrical in the future. The inaugural class at Trousdale Turner began their courses in March 2025, with classes being offered to additional participants throughout the past year. “This program is a gamechanger for incarcerated individuals. It offers them a tangible path to success, with the skills and certifications they need to secure meaningful employment after their release,” said Jonathan Smallwood, vice president of TCAT Hartsville. By collaborating with TCAT Hartsville, participants gain access to a vast catalog of programming and credentials that will support their continued personal and professional growth, even after their release. The program not only benefits the participants but also strengthens the community by ensuring that those reentering society are equipped with the skills necessary to succeed. The program operates on-site at Trousdale Turner, offering both classroom instruction and hands-on training. “I’m honored to be part of this initiative. It’s incredibly rewarding to help these individuals develop valuable skills that will open doors for them once they’re released. This is more than just a job—it’s a chance to make a real difference,” says TCAT Hartsville instructor Danny Allen. Participants who complete TCAT programming will receive industry-recognized certifications. Similar programs will eventually be offered at all four CoreCivic facilities in Tennessee, allowing residents to earn college-level programming credit in addition to vocational certifications.

title: Norra vs NikoHealth for Skilled Nursing Rentals
summary: Norra vs NikoHealth for skilled nursing: NikoHealth runs the DME supplier's billing and delivery business, while Norra gives facilities room-level tracking to cut their own rental spend.
body_text: If you are comparing Norra and NikoHealth, the first thing to know is that they are not really competitors. They sit on opposite sides of the same transaction. NikoHealth is business software for durable medical equipment suppliers, the companies that rent and deliver equipment to patients and facilities. Norra is built for the skilled nursing facility on the receiving end, the one paying the invoices. Both are good at what they do. They just do not do the same job, and confusing them costs a skilled nursing operator money. That distinction is the whole point of this piece. When a rented low-air-loss mattress or wound-therapy pump arrives at your building, a supplier on the other end is managing that order. NikoHealth is the kind of platform that supplier runs to process the order, route the delivery, and generate the bill you receive. Norra is the platform you run to see where that mattress ends up, confirm when the resident no longer needs it, and get it returned before it keeps billing. One tool bills you. The other helps you stop paying. Why the facility side is where the money is For a skilled nursing operator, rentals are the single largest equipment leak. A facility keeps paying a daily rate on a rented unit long after the resident stopped needing it, because nobody can confirm the unit is sitting unused in a storage room. Under Medicare's SNF consolidated billing rules, most equipment used during a covered Part A stay is bundled into the facility's per-diem, so the building, not Medicare, eats that rental cost directly ( CMS SNF consolidated billing ). A typical 110-bed nursing home loses six figures a year this way. With the median skilled nursing facility running on a 1.8 percent operating margin , that waste can equal most of a building's annual profit. We break the full cost model down in the 2026 SNF equipment waste report . None of that leak is visible from the supplier's software, and it is not supposed to be. NikoHealth's job is to make the supplier's billing accurate and their operation efficient. Your job is to stop paying for equipment you do not need, and that requires seeing your own floors. What NikoHealth is, and where it genuinely wins NikoHealth is a well-built, cloud-based platform for HME and DME providers, and for that audience it is a capable, modern system. It runs the full supplier business in one place, from patient intake through order-to-cash. Its billing and revenue-cycle module handles electronic claims, clean-claim scrubbing, insurance eligibility verification, payer contract and fee-schedule tracking, denials, and patient collections. Its rental management includes automated recurring invoice generation with Medicare capped-rental logic built in, flagging the 13-month cap so the supplier does not bill past it ( capped-rental rules, CMS ). It is strong on the operational side too. Inventory tracks goods across warehouses, delivery teams, and patients with barcode scanning and automated purchase orders. Its delivery app gives drivers route optimization, real-time navigation, proof of delivery with e-signature, and on-site payment collection. It layers on automated resupply for consumables, a full patient record, analytics, and integrations with Salesforce, PowerBI, and Tableau. It maintains HIPAA, AICPA, and ISO compliance. The honest credit: if you run a DME or HME supply business, NikoHealth is a real contender that does exactly what you need. Norra does none of this, and this piece will not pretend otherwise. On supplier billing, claims, fleet inventory, and delivery logistics, NikoHealth wins, because that is the business it was built for. Where a supplier platform cannot help the facility The gap opens the moment the question becomes "where is our equipment right now, and are we paying for something we already own." A supplier's inventory system models its own warehouse-to-patient pipeline. It knows what it shipped you and what it is billing you for. It does not, and cannot, show a skilled nursing operator a live, room-level map of every item moving around its building, because it has no visibility inside your walls. That blind spot is exactly where facility rental waste lives. Catching a rental that should have gone back depends on knowing the live location and status of every billable item without asking anyone to do anything. Nurses and aides already lose 30 to 60 minutes per shift hunting for equipment, and they are not going to stop and scan a barcode every time a pump rolls to a new room. So on the facility side, the location never gets updated, and the rental keeps billing. A supplier billing platform, however good, cannot close that gap for you. That is the workflow Norra automates, and we walk through it in how software stops duplicate rentals . Norra vs NikoHealth, head to head Norra is the facility-side tool. Proprietary smart tags report room-level location automatically through plug-in gateways, with no wiring, no scanning, and no capital install. Because the map stays current on its own, rental elimination, loss prevention, and cross-facility sharing run on live data instead of on whoever remembered to update a record. It adds skilled-nursing-specific tools a supplier platform does not carry: exit detection, one-click survey audit reports, and find-by-text search such as "where are the bariatric wheelchairs." Across a multi-facility skilled nursing network, Norra cut equipment spending by as much as 70 percent, drove 90 percent fewer new rental orders per month, saved over 1,100 staff hours a year, and brought unnecessary rentals to zero. Best for: skilled nursing facilities and chains that want to cut their own rental spend and find every item in real time. NikoHealth is the supplier-side tool. It is a strong, all-in-one platform for a DME or HME provider running intake, billing, claims, fleet inventory, and deliveries. It is not a facility-side location system, and it is not designed to help the building that receives the equipment cut what it pays. Best for: durable medical equipment suppliers and home medical equipment businesses managing their own rental fleet, revenue cycle, and delivery operation. Side-by-side comparison Capability Norra NikoHealth Whose business it runs The facility that owns and rents equipment The DME supplier that rents equipment out Automatic room-level equipment location inside a facility ✅ Automatic, always current ❌ Not a location system Staff scanning required ✅ None, fully automatic Barcode scanning by supplier staff Supplier billing, claims, and revenue cycle Not a billing platform, by design ✅ Core strength Multi-location fleet inventory and purchase orders Tracks the facility's own floors ✅ Warehouse to delivery to patient Delivery routing and proof of delivery Not a logistics tool ✅ Route optimization and mobile POD Medicare capped-rental billing logic Facility-side: flags rentals to return before they cost more ✅ Supplier-side capped-rental billing Helps a skilled nursing facility cut its own rental spend ✅ Flags rentals to return, kills duplicate rentals ❌ Runs the supplier's side of the bill Survey-ready equipment audit reports for an SNF ✅ One click ❌ Not shaped for facility surveys Install footprint Plug-in gateways, live in days Cloud software for the supplier's team Pricing model Operating expense, no capital install Supplier software subscription Read the table honestly. NikoHealth genuinely wins on supplier billing, claims, fleet inventory, and delivery logistics, because that is its purpose and it does it well. Norra wins on the things that decide whether a skilled nursing facility keeps its money: room-level location that is always current with zero scanning, a rental-elimination workflow that runs on that live data, survey-ready audit reports, and a price shaped like an operating budget instead of a capital project. The difference is not that one product is better made. It is that one runs the supplier's business and one runs the facility's. Can you use both, or neither You may well interact with both. Your rental suppliers might run NikoHealth or something like it on their end, and that is fine. It has nothing to do with what you deploy inside your building. Norra works alongside whatever software your suppliers use and any EHR you run. The mistake is assuming that because a supplier has good software, your rental spend is under control. It is not, because that software optimizes their invoice, not your return. The bottom line Choose Norra if you operate a skilled nursing facility or chain and want to cut what you pay: room-level tracking with zero scanning, rental elimination, loss prevention, exit detection, and one-click survey reports, live in days with no upfront cost. NikoHealth is the right pick if you are a durable or home medical equipment supplier and need to run your own intake, billing, claims, fleet inventory, and deliveries in one platform. For a nursing home trying to lower its rental bill, that split is the entire decision. A supplier's billing platform is the right tool for the supplier and the wrong tool for you, because the rentals you are trying to catch depend on live location inside your own walls that no one has to scan for. If you want to see your own equipment on a live map instead, start with a single-facility pilot at norra.io .

title: Mastercard MMSP: What Acquirers and PayFacs Need to Do Before July 2026
summary: Mastercard's MMSP rules are already in effect, with first reports due July 2026. Learn how acquirers and PayFacs can prepare now.
body_text: Mastercard’s June 2026 bulletin clarified the operational requirements under its Merchant Monitoring Service Provider standards , including how acquirers should use approved MMSPs, submit reports, and evidence ongoing monitoring activity. The underlying monitoring obligations were already substantively effective as of January 1, 2026. For merchants onboarded on or after that date, acquirers must complete an initial scan before the merchant begins processing Mastercard transactions. The first monthly reporting cycle under the clarified framework falls due in July, so acquirers should use the bulletin as an implementation checkpoint rather than treating July as the start of the obligation. ‍ ‍ ‍ What Is the MMSP and What Did Mastercard Clarify? ‍ The Merchant Monitoring Service Provider (MMSP) program sits under Mastercard's Business Risk Assessment and Mitigation (BRAM) program . Its purpose is to give acquirers a structured, third-party mechanism for monitoring merchant websites for prohibited content, transaction laundering activity, and other violations of Mastercard's acceptable use policies. ‍ The June 2026 bulletin clarified four operational requirements under the MMSP standard, rather than creating entirely new obligations. ‍ MMSP must be Mastercard-approved. Acquirers cannot designate internal scanning tools or unapproved third parties to fulfill the MMSP requirement. The provider must appear on Mastercard's published list of approved MMSPs. ‍ An initial scan is required before processing begins. For merchants onboarded on or after January 1, 2026, the MMSP must complete an initial review of the merchant’s digital footprint before the merchant begins processing Mastercard transactions. ‍ URL monitoring must cover members-only areas. Prior practice focused on publicly visible pages. The MMSP framework requires ongoing monitoring that extends into authenticated or gated content on merchant websites. This matters because prohibited content is frequently concealed behind login walls rather than on publicly indexed pages. ‍ Reports must be MMSP-authored and unaltered. Acquirers who forward monthly or incident reports to Mastercard must transmit them exactly as received from the MMSP. Internal annotation, summarization, or reformatting is not permitted. ‍ ‍ ‍ Who Needs to Comply? ‍ The primary obligation falls on acquirers : financial institutions and processors that hold a direct Mastercard membership and board merchants under that membership. ‍ Payment facilitators (PayFacs) do not carry a direct compliance obligation to Mastercard under this standard. However, their sponsoring acquirer does, and that acquirer's MMSP program must extend to cover PayFac sub-merchants . PayFacs need to understand their sponsoring acquirer's MMSP configuration and ensure their own merchant onboarding and monitoring processes align with it. ‍ Network Enablement Partners and Branded Processors are also in scope. If your organization touches Mastercard transaction routing and boards merchants in any capacity, confirm your compliance posture with your legal and compliance team. ‍ One practical implication for PayFacs: if your sponsoring acquirer has not yet opted into the MMSP program, the fine relief protections available to registered participants do not extend to your portfolio. This is a risk worth assessing now, not after the first reporting cycle. ‍ ‍ ‍ The Full MMSP Compliance Checklist ‍ The following nine steps represent the complete operational sequence for acquirers implementing the clarified MMSP framework. ‍ Step 1: Opt in to the MMSP program. Participation is structured as an opt-in. Acquirers that do not opt in forfeit the 75% fine relief available to registered participants. Non-participation does not exempt an acquirer from Mastercard's broader merchant monitoring obligations. ‍ Step 2: Select a Mastercard-approved MMSP. The MMSP must appear on Mastercard's approved provider list. Acquirers may work with more than one MMSP, which can be appropriate for portfolio segmentation or geographic coverage needs. ‍ Step 3: Submit merchant data to the MMSP. Once contracted, the acquirer submits merchant data, including URLs, business descriptors, and known digital identifiers, to the MMSP. The completeness of this data set directly affects scan coverage. ‍ Step 4: Complete the initial scan before transaction processing. For merchants onboarded on or after January 1, 2026, the MMSP must finish an initial web analysis before that merchant can begin processing Mastercard transactions. For acquirers with high-volume merchant boarding, this creates a workflow dependency that should be reflected in both MMSP contract SLAs and internal onboarding tooling. ‍ Step 5: Maintain continuous URL monitoring , including members-only areas. After initial onboarding, monitoring continues on an ongoing basis. This includes publicly accessible pages and authenticated or gated areas of the merchant's website. ‍ Step 6: MMSP reports violations within 5 business days. When the MMSP identifies a policy violation, it must report that finding to the acquirer within 5 business days of detection. Review your MMSP contract to confirm this SLA is explicitly stated and enforceable. ‍ Step 7: Acquirer investigates and resolves within 15 calendar days. Upon receiving a violation report, the acquirer has 15 calendar days to investigate and reach a resolution. Resolution may mean remediation with the merchant, suspension of processing, or termination. This window applies from the date of the MMSP's notification, not from when the acquirer internally triages the report. ‍ Step 8: Submit monthly MMSP-generated reports to Mastercard. Every month, the acquirer submits a report to Mastercard covering all enrolled merchants. This report must be generated by the MMSP. If the acquirer forwards it, it must be transmitted unaltered. ‍ Step 9: Apply MATCH system compliance where applicable. Where violations result in merchant termination, MATCH (Mastercard Alert to Control High-Risk Merchants) reporting obligations apply. MMSP enrollment provides documented evidence that the acquirer followed a structured monitoring process. ‍ ‍ ‍ ‍ Key Deadlines and Timelines ‍ ‍ A clarification worth noting for planning purposes: the June 2026 bulletin clarified the MMSP framework and reporting workflow. The underlying merchant monitoring obligations were already substantively effective as of January 1, 2026, while July 2026 is when the first monthly reporting cycle under the clarified framework falls due. ‍ Compliance teams should treat July as an operational reporting milestone, not the start of the obligation. ‍ ‍ ‍ ‍ Fines and Consequences ‍ Mastercard's specific fine schedules for MMSP-related violations are contained in the Security Rules and Procedures manual , which is available to acquirers through their Mastercard membership agreements and relationship contacts, but is not publicly available. ‍ What the bulletin makes clear is the consequence of participating versus not participating. ‍ Acquirers enrolled with a registered MMSP receive 75% fine relief on assessments related to covered violations. This is the program's most significant financial incentive. An acquirer that opts in, enrolls merchants, and follows the reporting workflow retains substantial protection against fine exposure when violations occur despite proper monitoring. ‍ Acquirers that do not opt in receive no fine relief. The full assessment applies on any qualifying violation. For portfolios with meaningful Mastercard volume, cumulative exposure over time represents a more significant risk than the operational cost of enrollment. ‍ Beyond financial assessments, consequences for repeated or unaddressed violations can include MATCH listing of merchants and, in more serious cases, risk to acquiring privileges. These outcomes are consistent with Mastercard's broader risk program structure. The absence of an MMSP enrollment record weakens an acquirer's compliance posture in any enforcement conversation. ‍ ‍ ‍ ‍ MMSP Reporting Requirements ‍ The reporting structure under the clarified MMSP framework has two components. ‍ ‍ Monthly reports cover the acquirer's enrolled merchant portfolio in full. Requirements include: ‍ The report must be generated by the MMSP, not the acquirer's internal team ‍ If the acquirer forwards the report to Mastercard, it must be transmitted unaltered ‍ The report must cover every enrolled merchant, not only those with findings ‍ Incident reports follow the same authorship requirement. When an MMSP identifies and reports a violation, that report document is the official record for Mastercard submission. Acquirers should not create parallel summaries or reformatted versions for submission. ‍ From an operational standpoint, this has real implications for how acquirers select and contract with an MMSP. Providers that generate structured outputs in a format compatible with Mastercard submission requirements reduce the compliance risk associated with manual handling. ‍ Providers that require acquirer staff to reformat or consolidate data before submission introduce both operational burden and compliance exposure. ‍ We recommend confirming during the MMSP evaluation process that the provider generates the monthly report directly from their platform and that the output format has been validated with Mastercard. This is worth specifying in the contract. ‍ ‍ ‍ How to Choose the Right MMSP ‍ Mastercard approval is the baseline requirement. Beyond that, acquirers evaluating MMSP options should assess the following criteria. ‍ Coverage depth, including members-only content. The MMSP framework requires monitoring of authenticated areas. Ask the provider to describe their methodology for accessing and scanning content behind login walls. This capability varies meaningfully across providers. ‍ Detection methodology. There is a real difference between keyword-based scanning and contextual web analysis that evaluates meaning across a merchant's full digital footprint. Keyword matching generates higher false positive rates and can miss violations phrased to avoid known trigger terms. Ask how the provider handles content that does not match a predefined term list. ‍ Language coverage. Merchants operating across jurisdictions may present content in a range of languages. An MMSP with language-agnostic digital footprint analysis provides more complete coverage than one dependent on supported language configurations. ‍ Native report generation. MMSP reports must be MMSP-authored. A provider whose platform generates the required monthly and incident report formats directly, without requiring acquirer-side reformatting, reduces both compliance risk and operational load. ‍ Speed and SLA terms. The initial scan SLA matters for onboarding velocity. The violation reporting SLA (the 5 business day window) should be contractually specified. Ask for historical performance data on both. ‍ API integration. Acquirers and PayFacs with significant boarding volume will want the MMSP to integrate with existing onboarding and case management workflows. Manual data submission at scale is not a sustainable approach for most portfolios. ‍ Risk level classification. Evaluation outputs should map to a structured risk level framework (low, medium, high, critical) that integrates with the acquirer's existing risk decisioning process. Ask how the provider defines and classifies findings. ‍ ‍ ‍ How Ballerine Supports MMSP Compliance ‍ Ballerine is a Mastercard-approved MMSP. Our web analysis capability covers both publicly visible and members-only merchant content, and our detection approach uses AI-based contextual analysis rather than keyword matching. This reduces false positives and improves coverage for content designed to avoid conventional scanning. ‍ Key operational features: ‍ Language-agnostic analysis covers merchant content in any language without additional configuration ‍ Automated Mastercard-format report generation with a median turnaround of approximately 10 minutes per merchant ‍ Native incident report output that meets the unaltered forwarding requirement ‍ API integration for acquirers and PayFacs incorporating MMSP checks into onboarding workflows ‍ Risk scoring structured around low, medium, high, and critical classifications ‍ For compliance teams managing the transition to the clarified MMSP framework, the platform handles registration, monitoring , and reporting requirements within a single workflow. If you want to see how it works in practice, we are available for a demonstration. ‍ ‍ Ballerine is a Mastercard-approved Merchant Monitoring Service Provider. This guide reflects publicly available information about the MMSP program structure and is intended for general informational purposes. Acquirers should review their Mastercard membership agreements and consult compliance counsel for guidance specific to their situation. ‍ ‍ ‍ ‍ ‍

title: AEP Texas Advances Reliability and Growth with Federal Funding Expected to Save Customers $685 Million
summary: AEP Texas, a subsidiary of American Electric Power, has entered into an agreement for a loan of up to $3.26 billion from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to help fund infrastructure investments to improve resiliency and deliver an estimated $685 million in total savings to customers over 30 years.
body_text: CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas (July 8, 2026) – AEP Texas, a subsidiary of American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP), has entered into an agreement for a loan of up to $3.26 billion from the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) to help fund infrastructure investments to improve resiliency and deliver an estimated $685 million in total savings to customers over 30 years. The loan is to finance a portfolio of nearly 100 projects to enhance grid reliability and support growth in one of the nation’s fastest growing regions. AEP Texas has signed letters of agreement (LOAs) supporting up to 41 gigawatts (GW) of potential new load additions through 2030. “Texas is poised for incredible growth over the next five years. AEP Texas is committed to enabling this opportunity, while leveraging resources to deliver future savings for our customers,” said Adrian Rodriguez, president and chief operating officer of AEP Texas. “This loan supports critical updates to our transmission infrastructure to strengthen reliability, connect new load and generation resources and manage affordability.” AEP Texas plans to use the funds to rebuild or reconductor existing transmission lines, as well as build new transmission lines, spanning approximately 2,800 miles. This investment is projected to increase capacity of existing transmission infrastructure and reduce power interruptions for customers. This loan is part of AEP’s broader strategy across its 11-state service territory to secure federal funding to reduce customer costs while supporting growth and investing in reliability and resiliency. # About AEP Texas AEP Texas is connected to over one million customers in the deregulated Texas retail electric marketplace. As an energy delivery (wires) company, AEP Texas delivers electricity safely and reliably to homes, businesses and industry across its nearly 100,000 square mile service territory in south and west Texas. AEP Texas also builds new power lines, restores service following outages and reads the meters via advanced meter technology for retail electric providers (REPs) throughout its service territory. The company also connects or disconnects service upon orders from the REPs. Connect with AEP Texas at AEPTexas.com, on Facebook and on X @aeptexas

body_text: The best invoicing software does more than generate invoices; it helps you get paid faster. Here's our pick of the best invoicing software for freelancers and businesses in the Philippines, with comparisons of features, pricing, and who each tool is best for. What to Look for in Invoicing Software Before jumping into the list, here's what actually matters when choosing invoicing software for a Philippine business: Philippine payment methods. Your invoicing tool is only useful if clients can pay through it. Look for software that supports GCash, Maya, credit cards, and online bank transfers, not just PayPal. Ease of use. You shouldn't need an accountant to send an invoice. The best tools let you create and send in under two minutes. Automatic reminders. The software should follow up on unpaid invoices for you, so you don't have to. Free tier or low cost. Most freelancers and small businesses don't need enterprise features. A free or affordable plan should cover basic invoicing needs. Payout speed. If the software collects payment, how quickly does that money reach your bank account? BIR compliance. Support for official receipt formats, CAS registration, and ideally EIS readiness for the 2026 mandate. Philippine tax handling. Automatic computation of VAT, percentage tax, withholding tax, not just a generic "tax rate" field. Filipino context. Designed around how Philippine businesses are structured: freelancers, sole proprietors, SMEs, BIR-registered corporations. The Best Philippine-Made and PH-Specific Invoicing Tools 1. PayMongo : Best for Getting Paid Instantly PayMongo isn't just invoicing software, but a full payment platform built specifically for Philippine businesses. When you send a PayMongo invoice, your client gets a professional payment page that accepts GCash, Maya, Visa, Mastercard, BPI Online, UnionBank, and over-the-counter payments. No separate payment step required. What it offers: Send an invoice link directly via chat, email, or SMS in minutes Clients pay via QR Ph, GCash, Maya, credit/debit cards, or bank transfer all in one place Automatic payment confirmation, no need to manually reconcile Payouts to your bank account in as fast as one business day No monthly fee; you only pay a transaction fee when you get paid BSP-licensed and PCI-DSS compliant Best for: Freelancers, service providers, SMEs, and microtax payers who need to get paid online, not just track invoices. However, as an invoicing tool alone, this is not recommended for e-commerce businesses or businesses/individuals under the large taxpayers group, due to the 2026 BIR E-Invoicing Mandate. If you’re part of that group, a compliance-focused tool with a financial infrastructure like PayMongo for payments. Pricing: No setup fee, no monthly fee. Transaction fees apply per payment received. See current rates . PayMongo is the only tool on this list built from the ground up for Philippine payment methods. If converting an invoice into an actual payment is your priority, this is where to start. Sign Up with PayMongo 2. Juan (by JuanTax) : Best All-in-One PH Accounting + Invoicing Juan is the product of a merger between JuanTax, the Philippines' first BIR-accredited electronic tax software provider (eTSP), and Singapore-based Jaz Philippines. The result is an automated accounting platform that handles invoicing, bookkeeping, tax filing, and financial reporting in one place. What it offers: BIR-accredited e-invoicing and official receipt generation Automated bookkeeping and real-time financial reports BIR tax filing (ITR, VAT, percentage tax, withholding tax) AI-powered transaction categorization Bank reconciliation EIS-ready for the 2026 mandate Best for: SMEs and growing businesses that want invoicing, accounting, and BIR compliance in a single platform. Pricing: Free plan: Limited users and features (no PH tax compliance, financial reports, and open APIs) Essentials (₱2,000/month): unlimited admins, up to 10 users, account management, cashflow reconciliation, etc. Growth (from ₱10,000/month): unlimited users, advanced AI agents, customized integrations, etc. See more of Juan’s pricing details here . 3. Taxumo: Best for Freelancers and Self-Employed Professionals Taxumo is a BIR-accredited online tax filing platform built specifically for Filipino freelancers, self-employed professionals, and small business owners. Its e-invoicing feature enables businesses to generate, send, and store invoices online. It also entails generating invoice data in a standardized structured format and preparing sales data for electronic reporting to the BIR. What makes Taxumo stand out for freelancers is its simplicity: it handles the BIR side of invoicing, such as official receipt formats, proper documentation, transition from manual ORs to e-invoices, without requiring accounting knowledge. What it offers: BIR-compliant e-invoicing Income and expense tracking (free) Automated tax computation (ITR, percentage tax, VAT) Online BIR filing and payment Guidance on receipt-to-invoice transition per current BIR rules Best for: Freelancers, consultants, and sole proprietors who want BIR compliance without hiring an accountant. Pricing: Free: includes income and expense tracking, and real time estimates. Doesn’t include tax form preparation, tax filing, or tax payment. 8% Plan (₱1,374/quarter): For non-VAT individuals using the 8% income tax rate. Includes preparation and filing support for applicable BIR forms (e.g., 1701Q, 1701A, 2551Q, 0605, SAWT). Micro plan (₱2,124/quarter): Also for non-VAT individuals under graduated tax rates, designed for businesses that also file withholding taxes (employees and/or suppliers), includes additional withholding tax forms and attachments. SMB Plan (₱2,749/quarter): For VAT-registered businesses, partnerships, and corporations. Includes VAT filing (2550Q), corporate income tax forms, withholding tax forms, and other compliance attachments. See more of Taxumo’s pricing details here . 4. N3 AI Accounting (formerly QNE): AI-Powered Accounting Software for Philippine Businesses N3 AI Accounting (formerly QNE AI Cloud Accounting) is a cloud-based accounting platform designed for Philippine SMEs. It is also 100% BIR CAS-approved and supports BIR-ready e-invoicing (EIS). The platform includes Quinny AI, an AI-powered assistant that helps automate bookkeeping tasks, categorize transactions, generate financial insights, and identify potential financial risks. It also features OCR-powered document scanning and can generate BIR forms, reports, certificates, and DAT files for tax compliance. What it offers: BIR CAS-approved accounting system with EIS-ready e-invoicing AI-assisted bookkeeping and transaction categorization (Quinny AI) BIR forms, reports, certificates, and DAT file generation OCR-powered document capture and data extraction Cloud-based accounting with real-time collaboration and mobile access ISO/IEC 27001:2022 security practices and role-based access controls Optional inventory, project, multi-location, and multi-currency modules on higher-tier plans Best for: SMEs and growing businesses that need a BIR CAS-compliant accounting system with AI-assisted bookkeeping and built-in support for Philippine tax and e-invoicing requirements. Pricing: Pricing: Basic: ₱900/month (annual billing) or ₱1,080/month Essential: ₱1,300/month (annual) or ₱1,600/month Professional: ₱1,800/month (annual) or ₱2,200/month Growth: ₱5,000/month (annual) or ₱6,000/month Enterprise: ₱10,000/month (annual) or ₱12,000/month For more details on N3 AI Accounting’s pricing, click here . Comparison: PH-Specific Invoicing Tools at a Glance Tool BIR Compliant PH Payments Tax Filing Best For PayMongo Invoicing only ✅ GCash, Maya, Cards, Banks ❌ Businesses that need to collect payments Juan ✅ BIR eTSP accredited Via PayMongo integration ✅ Full BIR filing SMBs needing accounting + tax + invoicing Taxumo ✅ BIR accredited No native ✅ Full BIR filing Freelancers + sole proprietors N3 AI / QNE ✅ BIR CAS + EIS ready No native ✅ BIR forms + DAT SMBs needing CAS compliance The 2026 BIR E-Invoicing Mandate: What You Need to Know The Philippine Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) is rolling out a mandatory Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) to modernize tax reporting and reduce manual tax compliance. Under the latest regulations, certain businesses must issue electronic invoices and transmit invoice data to the BIR using approved e-invoicing software by December 31, 2026 . What is the BIR Electronic Invoicing System (EIS)? The EIS is the BIR's digital platform for receiving, validating, and storing invoice data. Instead of simply generating PDF invoices or printed receipts, businesses will be required to create invoices in a structured electronic format (typically JSON) and electronically transmit the sales data to the BIR through an accredited system or API. Who needs to comply? The mandate initially applies to: Businesses engaged in e-commerce or online transactions (except micro taxpayers) Businesses under the BIR Large Taxpayers Service (LTS) Taxpayers classified as Large Taxpayers under the Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act Businesses using Computerized Accounting Systems (CAS), Computerized Books of Accounts (CBA) with electronic invoicing, or other invoicing software capable of producing structured invoice data. Major corporations with annual sales above ₱1 billion If you're in this group, global invoicing tools alone won't cut it. You need a platform that generates BIR-compliant JSON invoices and can transmit them to the EIS. Micro and small taxpayers not covered by the mandate can still voluntarily issue BIR-compliant e-invoices, and doing so early puts you ahead when the mandate eventually expands. Other taxpayer groups, such as exporters, certain incentive-registered businesses, and POS users, are expected to be covered in later phases once the BIR issues additional regulations. The Real Problem: Invoicing vs. Getting Paid Here's something most invoicing software guides don't say clearly enough: sending an invoice and getting paid are two different things. Most invoicing tools are great at the first part, creating a professional document, logging it, and sending reminders. But they leave the actual payment step to you, which usually means waiting for a bank transfer or following up manually. The tools that close this gap are the ones that let your client pay directly from the invoice – right then, in the moment, without any friction. For Philippine businesses, this means your invoicing tool needs to accept GCash, Maya, and cards natively. Otherwise, you're still chasing payments, just with nicer paperwork. How Payment Integration Fits Into the PH Invoicing Stack One pattern that works well for Philippine businesses: pair a compliance-focused tool with a financial OS like PayMongo for payments. Here's why: tools like Juan and Taxumo are excellent at BIR compliance, tax filing, and accounting, but their payment collection options are limited. A financial infrastructure such as PayMongo fills that gap by giving your clients a direct, frictionless way to pay via GCash, Maya, or card. The combination: Juan or Taxumo – handles your BIR invoicing, official receipts, and tax filings PayMongo – handles actual payment collection, instant confirmation, and next-day payout This is especially useful for freelancers and small businesses who need both compliance and fast cash flow. Create a Free PayMongo Account Frequently Asked Questions What is BIR EIS and when does it take effect? The BIR Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) is a centralized platform where covered taxpayers must transmit their sales invoices and receipts in BIR-compliant JSON format. The first group of covered taxpayers, large taxpayers, e-commerce businesses, and CAS/CBA users, must comply by December 31, 2026. Which Philippine invoicing software is BIR accredited? Juan (formerly JuanTax) is the Philippines' first BIR-accredited electronic tax software provider (eTSP). Taxumo is also BIR-accredited for tax filing and e-invoicing. N3 AI Accounting (QNE) holds BIR CAS approval and is EIS-ready. Can I use global tools like QuickBooks or Wave for BIR compliance? Global tools are not designed for BIR's specific requirements; they don't generate the correct JSON format for EIS transmission or produce BIR-standard forms. You'd need to pair them with a locally accredited solution, or switch to a PH-built platform to be safe for the 2026 mandate. Does PayMongo generate BIR-compliant invoices? PayMongo's invoicing is designed for payment collection, not BIR tax compliance. For official receipts and BIR-mandated e-invoices, use a BIR-accredited platform like Juan or Taxumo. Pair it with PayMongo for payment collection on those same invoices. What's the difference between an e-invoice and a payment link? An e-invoice is a BIR-compliant document that records a transaction for tax purposes. A payment link (like PayMongo's) is a way for clients to pay you online. You need both: the e-invoice for BIR, and the payment link so your client can actually pay without going to the bank. title: Search Interest in Accepting Digital Payments Surges Beyond NCR – Nearly Triple in Five Years

body_text: Search interest in accepting digital payments grew fastest in Northern Mindanao, Western Visayas and Davao in 2025 – outpacing Metro Manila roughly 3-5.5x – and kept climbing into 2026. Interest in digital payment acceptance among businesses outside Metro Manila has reached its highest level in five years, according to PayMongo's analysis of Google Trends data. The study underscores growing demand for digital payment solutions across Philippine provinces. Across major provincial regions, search interest in payment-acceptance terms – including "accept maya,” "accept gcash,” “accept qrph,” and “accept payments online” – has nearly tripled since 2022, with search interest in the first half of 2026 running 177% above the same period in 2022, on average across Central Luzon, Western Visayas, Central Visayas and the Davao Region. But the growth has accelerated sharply since 2025. Payment-acceptance search interest rose 238% year-over-year in Northern Mindanao, 192% in Western Visayas and 130% in the Davao Region, compared with 43% in the National Capital Region. Search interest in "gcash qr" reached its five-year peak in Western Visayas in May 2026, in Northern Mindanao in October 2025 and in the Davao Region in April 2025. From shoppers to sellers Searches for shopping platforms such as Shopee and Lazada declined 37% between the first half of 2022 and the first half of 2026 as post-pandemic e-commerce behavior normalized and moved in-app. The decline does not mean Filipinos are shopping less online; rather, the two-marketplace era is giving way to a more fragmented landscape. Challenger platforms' share of shopping searches grew 5x since 2022, and the parallel surge in payment-acceptance searches suggests a growing cohort of sellers transacting outside the big marketplaces entirely, perhaps through social channels, their own online stores and in-store QR, where accepting payments directly becomes essential. PayMongo's mid-year data shows the same trend: completed transactions across its merchant network grew 89% from H1 2025 to H1 2026, with its merchant base nearly doubling (+93%) over the same period. In the Davao Region, breakout growth in searches for platform "seller center" tools, alongside rising "accept gcash" interest across provinces, indicates provincial Filipinos are increasingly setting up shop online, not just buying. Meanwhile, early signs of a new entrepreneurship cycle are also appearing in the capital: searches for "online business ideas," "how to sell online" and related terms in Metro Manila grew 59% in the first half of 2026 versus the same period in 2025. The analysis also found an emerging second wave of QR adoption: search interest in "maya qr," minimal before 2024, has since multiplied in Metro Manila, Central Luzon, and Central Visayas, suggesting QR payments are becoming a multi-provider habit consistent with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas' QR Ph interoperability agenda. Start Accepting Payments Provincial shoppers embrace challenger platforms Provincial e-commerce is also diversifying. Challenger platforms like TikTok Shop, Temu, and Facebook Marketplace grew from roughly 2% of shopping-platform searches in 2022 to 8–13% today, with Eastern Visayas (13%), Central Visayas and Davao (12% each) ahead of Metro Manila (10%). Mega-sale culture also held: the November–December search lift around 11.11 and 12.12 sales remained steady or strengthened in most regions between 2022 and 2025. Conclusion Five years of Google Trends data show the Philippines' digital commerce boom didn't end after the pandemic. Instead, it changed form and moved south. Shopping-platform searches declined everywhere as browsing normalized, but digital payment-acceptance searches nearly tripled between 2022 and early 2026 in provincial regions, growing three to five times faster in Northern Mindanao, Western Visayas, and Davao in 2025 than in Metro Manila, and climbing further still in every region measured in the first half of 2026. Methodology Analysis is based on Google Trends monthly search-interest data for the period July 2021 to June 2026, retrieved July 16, 2026, for nine Philippine regions: NCR, Calabarzon, Central Luzon, Western Visayas, Central Visayas, Eastern Visayas, Northern Mindanao, Davao Region, and BARMM. Google Trends values are normalized (0–100) within each region and term set; figures reflect relative search interest, not absolute search volumes. Provincial growth rates are computed from lower absolute search-interest baselines than NCR's; part of the provincial–NCR growth differential reflects base effects typical of earlier-stage adoption. The payment-acceptance cluster comprises eight terms: "gcash qr," "maya qr," "accept gcash," "accept maya," "accept qrph," "accept qr ph," "accept online payment" and "accept payment online." The shopping cluster comprises Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop, Temu and Facebook Marketplace. The online-business cluster comprises eight terms including "how to sell online," "online business ideas," "how to start online business" and "online negosyo ." Within the dataset, 2021 covers July–December and 2026 covers January–June; partial-month data for July 2026 was excluded. Year-over-year comparisons use complete calendar years (2022–2025), while 2026 comparisons match January–June 2026 against the same months of the comparison year. Regional index averages use the four regions with statistically meaningful 2022 baselines. Northern Mindanao is excluded from the 2022-indexed average because its 2022 baseline falls below the reliability threshold; its year-over-year figures compare 2025 against 2024, where baseline volumes are sufficient. About PayMongo PayMongo Group is a fintech company that provides a financial operating system for growing businesses in the Philippines. It enables merchants to accept payments, move money, and borrow capital through a single, unified platform. From startups and SMEs to enterprises, thousands of Filipino merchants across retail, food, e-commerce, and services trust PayMongo to run their financial infrastructure. PayMongo is regulated by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) and is PCI-DSS 4.0 and SOC 2 Type 2 certified.

title: What’s New: MTurk closes to new customers, new 'Active in the last x days' filter, and more
summary: Filter participants by recent activity, see demographic breakdowns of your groups, configure AI Task Builder layouts, and more
body_text: From the new ‘Active in the last x days’ filter to demographic breakdowns of participant groups, this month’s updates take your data collection further. Scroll down to explore what’s new. Amazon MTurk is no longer accepting new customers from 30th July 2026 Amazon MTurk will stop accepting new customers from 30 July 2026. If you know researchers who are still using MTurk, or splitting recruitment between MTurk and Prolific, now's a good time to point them our way. First-time Prolific researchers can redeem a £50 coupon through 30 July. Find out more We've also put together a full breakdown of how Prolific and MTurk compare here . These are some of the key differences. Data quality: Prolific has consistently delivered higher data quality compared to MTurk across multiple research studies. See the evidence . Lower cost per quality response: A recent preprint found that Prolific's cost per high-quality respondent was $5.68 versus $93.33 for MTurk, once data quality is accounted for. Similar analysis by Douglas et al in 2023 found that Prolific cost roughly half what MTurk cost once quality was factored in. Prolific is built for quality research, by researchers: We're continually shipping new features to help you run better studies, from Authenticity Checks (to catch AI-generated responses and bots) to Longitudinal Projects (to run multi-wave studies), alongside a steadily growing participant pool. Know a researcher this could help? Send them straight to the coupon page before 30 July. Target your study to only active participants If your study setup typically uses participant groups or saved filter sets, some of the participants who matched last time may be less active today. Until now, there hasn’t been a way to filter for activity directly. The new ‘Active in the last X days’ filter does this for you. Narrow down the last time a participant was active in the platform, which includes logging in, viewing their dashboard or taking a study. Add it to your study’s filters, combine it with an existing participant group, or save it as part of an existing filter set so your study reaches people those who are genuinely active on the platform. This means that you can reuse participant groups or saved filter sets without the need to prune or rebuild manually, as less active participants simply won’t be included. Explore in platform or via API Know the demographic breakdowns of your participant groups More Participant Group Hub uplifts this month! Now, you can analyse any participant group directly in the Overview tab. Pick a demographic filter like age, marital status or more and get the percentage and actual count breakdown of your group. Explore different filters for rich insights to learn even more about your participant group. It means you can sanity-check a group against what your study needs before you launch, especially important if you use groups across teams or studies. Currently available in the UI , with API support coming soon. Head to the Participants tab in Prolific to explore these updates → Configure your task layout in AI Task Builder, with more flexibility to come Where your stimulus sits, which questions appear alongside it and how the screen is split are critical layout decisions that shape how well participants can complete a task. Instead of a fixed structure, AI Task Builder now lets you define the layout for your task. Each page is built from rows, and each row can hold up to two columns. Put your stimulus in one column and your questions in the next for a clean side-by-side layout, or stack a dataset field above supporting context for something more guided. Each column can hold: A dataset field (image, text, audio, etc.) An instruction (radio buttons, free text, text with unit selection, file uploads) A content block for supporting copy Mix and match to build side-by-side comparisons, structured annotation tasks, and more. Unsure how to get started? Explore the new functionality with these ready-made GitHub repos: Prolific Smart Glasses POV Video Collection AI-Task-Builder-Image-Collection AI-Task-Builder-Free-Text-Collection This is the first step in a series of flexibility improvements in AI Task Builder, watch this space for more! Available now via API for AI Task Builder Batches (annotation tasks). More verified Experts available for your next study Our Network reaches over 330,000 90-day active participants so far this month. Standout growth in our Expert Network - our specialist participants individually verified for their skills or expertise. 1,200 new language specialists every month From major languages to niche dialects, our verified language experts are CEFR-certified across 4 core skills: Over 1,000 specialists in major languages such as Spanish (1520+) German (1340+), with Mandarin (890+) closely behind Emerging coverage across Telugu (265+), Tamil (180+) and Gujarati (35+). If specific dialects is a priority for your research, explore the variety in our Network today. Verified healthcare professionals Our Network now contains over 700 verified doctors across 35 clinical specialities. We cross-check licenses and credentials against official registries to qualify entry. Top specialties in this group currently are paediatrics, internal medicine, emergency medicine and psychiatry. This segment is actively growing, with other healthcare professions such as nurses (345+), mental health professionals (65+), pharmacists (45+) and more. If you need professionals from a specific field, find them in-app under Participants > Add screeners > Domain Experts . To find them under the API, take a look here . Use our Audience Finder to check if your audience is on Prolific. Watch: New episodes of The Frontier Series The Frontier Series continues with two new episodes recorded at ICLR 2026 in Rio de Janeiro. Our AI research engineers Nora Petrova and John Burden sit down with Henry Conklin (Princeton) and Tom Hosking (Cohere) to unpack their paper "Learning is Forgetting: LLM Training as Lossy Compression" . Episode 4 digs into what forgetting reveals about how models learn, and Episode 5 explores what this means for how we train, evaluate and select models. Use AND / OR logic in saved filter sets When you need to target a complex audience, AND / OR logic lets you define multiple conditions. Now, you can apply the same logic to a Filter Set and within nested groups, for more precise targeting (e.g. Employed = full-time OR part-time AND Age = 18-25). This saves you time from manually applying filters each time, especially useful if you run multiple studies with the same criteria. Try it now in the UI and the API . Quality of life updates this month Fetch cleaner message results via the API. If your integration sends automated messages to participants (like return requests or warnings), you can now exclude those from your results when polling GET /api/v1/messages/ . Use the new excluded_sender_ids parameter to pass a comma-separated list of user IDs, so you only get back genuine participant replies. Find your sender ID , then get started with filtering your messages . Search all filters from any tab. Search is now available on all tabs (Premium, Popular, All) and searches the entire catalogue at once, not just the tab you’re viewing. Streamlining our terminology . “Screener” and “Prescreener” are now called “Filter” in the UI, to align with the language in the API. This means that across the UI and API: Filters: the criteria you use to target participants for a study (e.g. age) Screeners: a custom screener study you launch to qualify participants before you invite them to your main study Meet the team in person Discover our Research at ICML A busy month for Prolific's AI research scientists as Nora Petrova and John Burden 's paper " Pressure Reveals Character " was accepted to ICML. The paper argues that many evaluations test what models know or claim, rather than how they behave when honesty, safety, deference or non-manipulation becomes costly. The team are also hosting a workshop at ICML: " Theory of Mind and Persuasion Beyond Conversation '' This study introduces a benchmark for evaluating whether LLM agents can plan actions that induce specific belief states in other agents. We’re heading to ISPP’s 2026 Annual Meeting Join Dr Andrew Gordon (Staff Researcher - Behavioural Science, Prolific) on 16 July at 10.30am, where he’ll present Not All Samples Are Created Equal: A Comprehensive Comparison of Online Sample Data Quality. Learn more and browse the full itinerary, click here . Say hello at the CARMA Summer Symposium On 22 July Dr Andrew Gordon will speak about data quality alongside panellists from Morning Consult and Longwood University from 10am to midday. Learn more here . Learn about data quality and AI at King’s Head to King’s Open Research Summer School on 24 July to hear from Emilio Noriega Farres (Senior Product Manager, Prolific) speak about data quality and AI. Register to join the session, or visit our booth for a demo. Find us at the 2026 Academy of Management Annual Meeting Register to hear from Dr Andrew Gordon , on 2nd August where he joins the panel at the 2026 Academy of Management Annual Meeting in Philadelphia to discuss Large Language Model Pollution in Online Behavioural Research. That’s all for our July update! See you next month. The Prolific team

title: From the Creators of ‘Parasyte: The Grey’: ‘Parasyte: TAMIYA’ Arrives 2027, Starring Shioli Kutsuna
body_text: Coming off a collaboration on Human Vapor , Netflix once again teams up with creator Yeon Sang-ho to expand the Parasyte universe with a new live-action series, Parasyte: TAMIYA , releasing in 2027. The series stars Shioli Kutsuna and reunites many of the key creatives behind Parasyte: The Grey . This new series tells the story of Ryoko Tamiya, a very levelheaded and “human” parasite who begins to question how, or if, parasites and humans can coexist. Seen through Tamiya’s eyes, the world of Parasyte becomes a lens on survival, identity and what it really means to be human. The original manga "Parasyte" (published by Kodansha) is a timeless masterpiece that ran from 1988 to 1995 and has been loved for more than 30 years, selling around 25 million copies across more than 20 countries and regions. “Parasyte” enthralled fans with its thrilling plot twists, dark setting and richly imaginative story infused with philosophical themes, and anime and film adaptations have carried its popularity across generations. In 2024, Parasyte: The Grey by Yeon Sang-ho ( Colony, The Ugly, Hellbound ), told a new story set in modern-day Korea based on the original manga, which is streaming globally on Netflix. It remained on the Global Top 10 Non-English Shows list for four weeks and ranked #1 in 34 countries, sparking a global Parasyte obsession. Parasyte: TAMIYA is the next evolution in that universe. In the original manga, Ryoko Tamiya is a parasite who takes over the body of a high school teacher and becomes an antagonist for Shinichi Izumi. Initially a brutal parasite that attacks humans indiscriminately, Tamiya learns a great deal about humanity through her job as a teacher. Upon seeing Shinichi and Migi sharing a body, she begins to think that coexistence with humanity will give her species the best chance at survival. The team behind Human Vapor and Parasyte: The Grey returns for this series. Yeon Sang-ho developed Parasyte: TAMIYA and wrote the script in collaboration with Ryu Yong-jae. WOWPOINT, which was the production company behind both aforementioned titles, was involved with development and production. Kensaku Kakimoto ( Glass Heart ) and Kazuhiro Nakagawa ( Double, Bullet Train Explosion ) direct the series. Yeon Sang-ho’s penchant for exposing the nature of people when placed in extreme situations, Kakimoto’s talent for music and visual storytelling and Nakagawa’s dynamic action and VFX production combine to create a new Parasyte story with significant promise. Shioli Kutsuna ( Sanctuary, Deadpool 2, Gundam ) plays Ryoko Tamiya in three distinct ways: the original human, the supposedly violent parasite, and the parasite who struggles to coexist with humanity. “She did a wonderful job of portraying the process of a non-human creature coming to understand both humanity and her own existence,” Yeon Sang-ho said in praise of her acting. Parasyte: TAMIYA streams worldwide in 2027, only on Netflix. Q&A with Yeon Sang-ho (Developed & Written by) Q: In these modern times, what kind of world did you want to depict through Tamiya’s perspective? A: Ryoko Tamiya is a truly captivating villain in the original manga. Her struggles over the nature of her own existence are what elevate the original “Parasyte” from a simple hero-based manga aimed at kids to something deeper. She’s a fascinating character, which drove me to want to tell the story of “Parasyte” through her perspective. I wanted to convey her perpetual struggle over the need for parasites to coexist with humans and the issue of their survival, and how she suffers setbacks and learns over time. I think the anguish she experiences is the essence of “Parasyte.” Q: Why did you choose Shioli Kutsuna to play the main character? A: In the manga, Ryoko Tamiya is a teacher in her twenties. Not only has Kutsuna played a wide variety of roles in both Japan and overseas, but she has also gained a deep understanding of the science fiction genre from American films and television series. I was very impressed with her version of Ryoko Tamiya. In this series, she plays three distinct versions of Ryoko Tamiya: the original human, the parasite after it takes over, and the parasite once it starts struggling with the issue of how to interact with humanity. I’m sure that was a big challenge for Kutsuna as an actor. I think she did a wonderful job of portraying the process of a non-human creature coming to understand both humanity and its own existence. Q: Why did you choose Kensaku Kakimoto and Kazuhiro Nakagawa as the directors? What did you expect from them, and what were your impressions of them during filming? A: Kensaku Kakimoto is a director with an exceptional talent for visual storytelling and with good taste in music. I was very excited to see his take on Parasyte, which could be considered the pinnacle of the body snatcher genre. Parasyte: Tamiya ended up exceeding my expectations. As for Kazuhiro Nakagawa, I noticed he had participated as a co-writer or director on many projects. He strikes me as a director who is skilled at getting to the heart of a story. I’m always amazed by the composition and production of each shot. I chose these two directors precisely because they have such different styles, and I had high hopes for a collaboration between them. Q: I believe the series is in the editing phase now that filming is complete. How do you feel about it? Please share a message for the fans who are awaiting its release. A: “Parasyte” is a legendary manga that has been adapted as a film series, an anime and a Korean drama. I am deeply honored to have been involved with this timeless masterpiece twice. This series, which is currently being edited, brings new things to the table compared to past entries in terms of story, cinematography, action, production, you name it. It firmly reflects the vision of both directors and is made with great respect for the original manga. I hope fans are excited to see it. Shioli Kutsuna Ryoko Tamiya is the most challenging role I have ever played in my acting career. During the six months I spent living as Tamiya, I experienced many emotions I had never encountered before. The role taught me a great deal and allowed me to grow not only as a person but also as an actor. Every day on set brought new discoveries and possibilities. As I portrayed Tamiya, I found myself constantly reflecting on the profound themes of the original manga, making the experience an incredibly rewarding one as an actor. This series was brought to life through the dedication of the entire cast and crew, who supported one another through every challenge along the way. It is a project that means a great deal to all of us, and I can't wait for audiences to experience it. Yoshihiro Sato (Netflix) "What makes a human?" "Can we coexist with beings that are different from us?" — These questions posed by "Parasyte" more than 30 years ago feel much more pressing for our modern society that has placed non-sentient AI at all of our fingertips. This series depicts the untold story of Ryoko Tamiya. Despite being a parasite who preyed upon and possessed the body of the human with the same name, the experience of raising a human baby and developing a bond with it inspires her to search for a way to coexist with humanity. Can one's innate nature be reshaped by experience? Tamiya's conflict and life journey are explored for the first time in this original story that stays true to the essence of the manga. Our purpose in making this series was to take the universal questions posed by the original manga 30 years ago and bring them into the modern spotlight. I hope everyone is excited to see yet another collaboration between Netflix and Yeon Sang-ho featuring the work of many excellent Japanese creators and actors.
